It is risky because the predicted miss distance is only about 412 m while the objects will be passing at roughly 14.2 km/s, giving a collision probability of 3.1 × 10⁻⁴ (about 1 in 3,226). Those numbers mean a small positional error could lead to impact, and the high relative speed makes any collision extremely energetic. The same pattern appears in the second conjunction: a miss distance of 690 m, relative speed 12.8 km/s, probability 8.7 × 10⁻⁵ (≈ 1 in 11,494). Both scenarios exceed safe thresholds, prompting avoidance options.
